docs.summary: Pulls this body toward a target pose relative to the connected body, or to the world without one, with a spring and a damper on its position and another pair on its rotation, each with a limit on how hard it may push. The spring closes the gap to the target pose and the damper matches the target velocity, both solved inside the physics solver, so a drive stays stable however stiff it is set and whatever else is jointed to the body. The position drive acts between this body's origin and the target point on the connected body, so each body is pushed at that point and turned by the push as a real joint would be. Directions a body cannot move or turn in are left out of the drive.
Where this body's origin is driven to, from the connected body's origin in its space, or in the world without one.
The rotation this body is driven to, relative to the connected body's, or in the world without one.
The velocity relative to the connected body the damper drives toward, in the connected body's space.
The angular velocity relative to the connected body the rotation damper drives toward, in the connected body's space.
The position spring, in newtons per metre of gap.
The position damper, in newtons per metre per second of speed off the target velocity.
The most the position drive pushes with, in newtons.
The rotation spring, in newton metres per radian of turn.
The rotation damper, in newton metres per radian per second of spin off the target.
The most the rotation drive twists with, in newton metres.
The push the position drive gave on the last substep, in newton seconds.
Gets the underlying Jitter2 constraint. Composite joints own several and return null here; anything that has to act on all of them goes through `GetConstraints`.
